title: How climate change affects your mental health | Britt Wray

blocks.en_text: For all that's ever been said about climate change,
blocks.zh_text: 关于气候变化，人们已经说了那么多，

blocks.en_text: we haven't heard nearly enough about the psychological impacts
blocks.zh_text: 但我们听到的关于心理影响的讨论还远远不够，

blocks.en_text: of living in a warming world.
blocks.zh_text: 也就是生活在一个不断变暖的世界里会带来什么心理影响。

blocks.en_text: If you've heard the grim climate research
blocks.zh_text: 如果你听过那些严峻的气候研究，

blocks.en_text: that science communicators like me weave into our books and documentaries,
blocks.zh_text: 也就是像我这样的科学传播者写进书和纪录片里的那些研究，

blocks.en_text: you've probably felt bouts of fear, fatalism or hopelessness.
blocks.zh_text: 你大概也感受过一阵阵的恐惧、宿命感或绝望。

blocks.en_text: If you've been impacted by climate disaster,
blocks.zh_text: 如果你亲身经历过气候灾害，

blocks.en_text: these feelings can set in much deeper,
blocks.zh_text: 这些感受会扎得更深，

blocks.en_text: leading to shock, trauma,
blocks.zh_text: 导致震惊、创伤、

blocks.en_text: strained relationships, substance abuse
blocks.zh_text: 关系紧张、药物滥用，

blocks.en_text: and the loss of personal identity and control.
blocks.zh_text: 以及失去自我认同和掌控感。

blocks.en_text: Vital political and technological work is underway to moderate our climate chaos,
blocks.zh_text: 重大的政治和技术工作正在推进，以缓解我们的气候混乱，

blocks.en_text: but I'm here to evoke a feeling in you
blocks.zh_text: 但我来这里是想让你真切地感受到，

blocks.en_text: for why we also need our actions and policies
blocks.zh_text: 为什么我们的行动和政策也需要

blocks.en_text: to reflect an understanding of how our changing environments
blocks.zh_text: 体现出这样一种理解：我们不断变化的环境

blocks.en_text: threaten our mental, social and spiritual well-being.
blocks.zh_text: 是如何威胁我们的心理、社交和精神健康的。

blocks.en_text: The anxiety, grief and depression of climate scientists and activists
blocks.zh_text: 气候科学家和活动人士的焦虑、悲伤和抑郁，

blocks.en_text: have been reported on for years.
blocks.zh_text: 多年来一直有报道。

blocks.en_text: Trends we've seen after extreme weather events
blocks.zh_text: 我们在极端天气事件之后看到的趋势，

blocks.en_text: like hurricane Sandy or Katrina
blocks.zh_text: 比如飓风桑迪或卡特里娜，

blocks.en_text: for increased PTSD and suicidality.
blocks.zh_text: 是创伤后应激障碍和自杀倾向的增加。

blocks.en_text: And there are rich mental-health data from northern communities
blocks.zh_text: 还有来自北方社区的丰富心理健康数据，

blocks.en_text: where warming is the fastest,
blocks.zh_text: 那里变暖速度最快，

blocks.en_text: like the Inuit in Labrador,
blocks.zh_text: 比如拉布拉多的因纽特人，

blocks.en_text: who face existential distress as they witness the ice,
blocks.zh_text: 他们目睹着冰——

blocks.en_text: a big part of their identity,
blocks.zh_text: 他们身份认同的重要部分——

blocks.en_text: vanishing before their eyes.
blocks.zh_text: 在眼前消失，承受着存在性的痛苦。

blocks.en_text: Now if that weren't enough,
blocks.zh_text: 如果这还不够，

blocks.en_text: the American Psychological Association
blocks.zh_text: 美国心理学会

blocks.en_text: says that our psychological responses to climate change,
blocks.zh_text: 表示，我们对气候变化的心理反应，

blocks.en_text: like conflict avoidance, helplessness and resignation, are growing.
blocks.zh_text: 比如回避冲突、无助感和认命，正在加剧。

blocks.en_text: This means that our conscious and unconscious mental processes
blocks.zh_text: 这意味着我们有意识和无意识的心理过程

blocks.en_text: are holding us back
blocks.zh_text: 正在阻碍我们

blocks.en_text: from identifying the causes of the problem for what they are,
blocks.zh_text: 认清问题的真正根源，

blocks.en_text: working on solutions and fostering our own psychological resilience,
blocks.zh_text: 去研究解决方案，并培养我们自己的心理韧性，

blocks.en_text: but we need all those things to take on what we've created.
blocks.zh_text: 而我们需要这一切来应对我们自己造成的局面。

blocks.en_text: Lately, I've been studying a phenomenon
blocks.zh_text: 最近，我一直在研究一种现象，

blocks.en_text: that's just one example of the emotional hardships
blocks.zh_text: 它只是我们所看到的情绪困境中的一个例子。

blocks.en_text: that we're seeing.
blocks.zh_text: 仅此而已。

blocks.en_text: And it comes in the form of a question
blocks.zh_text: 它以一个问题的形式出现，

blocks.en_text: that a significant amount of people in my generation are struggling to answer.
blocks.zh_text: 我这一代有很多人都难以回答这个问题。

blocks.en_text: That being:
blocks.zh_text: 那就是：

blocks.en_text: Should I have a child in the age of climate change?
blocks.zh_text: 在气候变化的时代，我该不该要孩子？

blocks.en_text: After all, any child born today
blocks.zh_text: 毕竟，今天出生的任何孩子

blocks.en_text: will have to live in a world where hurricanes, flooding, wildfires --
blocks.zh_text: 都将生活在一个飓风、洪水、野火——

blocks.en_text: what we used to call natural disasters --
blocks.zh_text: 我们过去称之为自然灾害的东西——

blocks.en_text: have become commonplace.
blocks.zh_text: 已经司空见惯的世界里。

blocks.en_text: The hottest 20 years on record occurred within the last 22.
blocks.zh_text: 有记录以来最热的20年都发生在过去22年里。

blocks.en_text: The UN expects that two-thirds of the global population
blocks.zh_text: 联合国预计，全球三分之二的人口

blocks.en_text: may face water shortages only six years from now.
blocks.zh_text: 可能仅仅六年后就会面临水资源短缺。

blocks.en_text: The World Bank predicts that by 2050,
blocks.zh_text: 世界银行预测，到2050年，

blocks.en_text: there's going to be 140 million climate refugees
blocks.zh_text: 将会有1.4亿气候难民

blocks.en_text: in sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America and South Asia.
blocks.zh_text: 出现在撒哈拉以南非洲、拉丁美洲和南亚。

blocks.en_text: And other estimates put that number at over one billion.
blocks.zh_text: 而其他估算认为这个数字超过十亿。

blocks.en_text: Mass migrations and resource scarcity
blocks.zh_text: 大规模移民和资源短缺

blocks.en_text: increase the risk for violence, war and political instability.
blocks.zh_text: 会增加暴力、战争和政治动荡的风险。

blocks.en_text: The UN just reported that we are pushing up to a million species to extinction,
blocks.zh_text: 联合国刚刚报告说，我们正把多达一百万种物种推向灭绝，

blocks.en_text: many within decades,
blocks.zh_text: 许多会在几十年内消失，

blocks.en_text: and our emissions are still increasing, even after the Paris Agreement.
blocks.zh_text: 而我们的排放量仍在增加，即便在《巴黎协定》之后也是如此。

blocks.en_text: Over the last year and a half,
blocks.zh_text: 在过去的一年半里，

blocks.en_text: I've been conducting workshops and interviews
blocks.zh_text: 我一直在举办工作坊和访谈，

blocks.en_text: with hundreds of people
blocks.zh_text: 和数百人交流，

blocks.en_text: about parenting in the climate crisis.
blocks.zh_text: 话题是在气候危机中养育孩子。

blocks.en_text: And I can tell you
blocks.zh_text: 我可以告诉你，

blocks.en_text: that people who are worried about having kids because of climate change
blocks.zh_text: 那些因为气候变化而担心要不要孩子的人

blocks.en_text: are not motivated by an ascetic pride.
blocks.zh_text: 并不是出于一种禁欲式的骄傲。

blocks.en_text: They're nerve-racked.
blocks.zh_text: 他们是焦虑不安的。

blocks.en_text: There's even a movement called BirthStrike,
blocks.zh_text: 甚至有一个叫BirthStrike的运动，

blocks.en_text: whose members have declared they're not going to have kids
blocks.zh_text: 其成员公开表示他们不打算要孩子，

blocks.en_text: because of the state of the ecological crisis
blocks.zh_text: 因为生态危机的现状，

blocks.en_text: and inaction from governments to address this existential threat.
blocks.zh_text: 也因为各国政府在应对这一生存威胁上的不作为。

blocks.en_text: And yes, other generations have also faced their own apocalyptic dangers,
blocks.zh_text: 没错，其他世代也面临过他们自己的末日式危险，

blocks.en_text: but that is no reason to disregard the very real threat to our survival now.
blocks.zh_text: 但这不能成为忽视我们当下所面临的真实生存威胁的理由。

blocks.en_text: Some feel that it's better to adopt children.
blocks.zh_text: 有些人觉得领养孩子更好。

blocks.en_text: Or that it's unethical to have more than one,
blocks.zh_text: 或者觉得生一个以上是不道德的，

blocks.en_text: especially three, four or more,
blocks.zh_text: 尤其是三个、四个甚至更多，

blocks.en_text: because kids increase greenhouse gas emissions.
blocks.zh_text: 因为孩子会增加温室气体排放。

blocks.en_text: Now, it is a really unfortunate state of affairs
blocks.zh_text: 现在，这真是一种令人遗憾的状况，

blocks.en_text: when people who want kids sacrifice their right to
blocks.zh_text: 当想要孩子的人牺牲了他们要孩子的权利，

blocks.en_text: because, somehow, they have been told that their lifestyle choices are to blame
blocks.zh_text: 因为不知怎么的，他们被告知要怪自己的生活方式选择，

blocks.en_text: when the fault is far more systemic,
blocks.zh_text: 而真正的过错要系统得多，

blocks.en_text: but let's just unpack the logic here.
blocks.zh_text: 但我们不妨来拆解一下这里的逻辑。

blocks.en_text: So an oft-cited study shows that, on average,
blocks.zh_text: 一项常被引用的研究表明，平均而言，

blocks.en_text: having one less child in an industrialized nation
blocks.zh_text: 在工业化国家少生一个孩子

blocks.en_text: can save about 59 tons of carbon dioxide per year.
blocks.zh_text: 每年可以节省约59吨二氧化碳。

blocks.en_text: While in comparison,
blocks.zh_text: 相比之下，

blocks.en_text: living car-free saves nearly 2.5 tons,
blocks.zh_text: 不开车能节省近2.5吨，

blocks.en_text: avoiding a transatlantic flight -- and this is just one --
blocks.zh_text: 避免一次跨大西洋飞行——而这只是一次——

blocks.en_text: saves about 1.5 tons,
blocks.zh_text: 能节省约1.5吨，

blocks.en_text: and eating a plant-based diet can save almost one ton per year.
blocks.zh_text: 而吃植物性饮食每年能节省近一吨。

blocks.en_text: And consider that a Bangladeshi child
blocks.zh_text: 再想想，一个孟加拉国的孩子

blocks.en_text: only adds 56 metric tons of carbon to their parents' carbon legacy
blocks.zh_text: 只给父母的碳遗产增加56公吨碳

blocks.en_text: over their lifetime,
blocks.zh_text: 在他们的一生中，

blocks.en_text: while an American child, in comparison, adds 9,441 to theirs.
blocks.zh_text: 而相比之下，一个美国孩子会给父母的碳遗产增加9441公吨。

blocks.en_text: So this is why some people argue
blocks.zh_text: 所以这就是为什么有些人主张

blocks.en_text: that it's parents from nations with huge carbon footprints
blocks.zh_text: 是那些来自碳足迹巨大国家父母

blocks.en_text: who should think the hardest about how many kids they have.
blocks.zh_text: 最应该认真考虑自己生几个孩子。

blocks.en_text: But the decision to have a child and one's feelings about the future
blocks.zh_text: 但要不要孩子这个决定，以及一个人对未来的感受

blocks.en_text: are deeply personal,
blocks.zh_text: 都是极其私人的事，

blocks.en_text: and wrapped up in all sorts of cultural norms,
blocks.zh_text: 还牵扯到各种各样的文化规范、

blocks.en_text: religious beliefs, socioeconomic status, education levels and more.
blocks.zh_text: 宗教信仰、社会经济地位、教育水平等等。

blocks.en_text: And so to some, this debate about kids in the climate crisis
blocks.zh_text: 所以对一些人来说，这场关于气候危机下要不要孩子的争论

blocks.en_text: can seem like it came from another planet.
blocks.zh_text: 简直像是从另一个星球来的。

blocks.en_text: Many have more immediate threats to their survival to think about,
blocks.zh_text: 很多人有更迫在眉睫的生存威胁要考虑，

blocks.en_text: like, how they're going to put food on the table,
blocks.zh_text: 比如怎么把饭端上桌，

blocks.en_text: when they're a single mom working three jobs,
blocks.zh_text: 当一个打三份工的单亲妈妈，

blocks.en_text: or they're HIV positive or on the move in a migrant caravan.
blocks.zh_text: 或者自己是HIV阳性，或者正跟着移民大篷车迁徙。

blocks.en_text: Tragically, though, climate change is really great at intersectionality.
blocks.zh_text: 但不幸的是，气候变化在交叉性方面真是厉害得很。

blocks.en_text: It multiplies the stresses marginalized communities already face.
blocks.zh_text: 它会放大边缘化群体本已承受的压力。

blocks.en_text: A political scientist once said to me that a leading indicator
blocks.zh_text: 一位政治学家曾对我说，一个领先指标

blocks.en_text: that climate change is starting to hit home, psychologically,
blocks.zh_text: 能说明气候变化开始在心理上真正影响到人们，

blocks.en_text: would be an increase in the rate of informed women
blocks.zh_text: 那就是越来越多了解情况的女性

blocks.en_text: deciding to not have children.
blocks.zh_text: 决定不生孩子。

blocks.en_text: Interesting.
blocks.zh_text: 有意思。

blocks.en_text: Is it hitting home with you, psychologically?
blocks.zh_text: 它是不是也在心理上影响到你了？

blocks.en_text: Are you perhaps someone with climate-linked pre-traumatic stress?
blocks.zh_text: 你会不会正经历与气候相关的创伤前压力？

blocks.en_text: A climate psychiatrist coined that term,
blocks.zh_text: 这个词是一位气候精神病学家创造的，

blocks.en_text: and that's a profession now, by the way, shrinks for climate woes.
blocks.zh_text: 顺便说一句，这现在是个职业了，专治气候烦恼的心理医生。

blocks.en_text: They're getting work at a time when some high schoolers
blocks.zh_text: 他们现在活儿不少，因为有些高中生

blocks.en_text: don't want to apply to university any longer,
blocks.zh_text: 已经不想申请大学了，

blocks.en_text: because they can't foresee a future for themselves.
blocks.zh_text: 因为他们看不到自己的未来。

blocks.en_text: And this brings me back to my main point.
blocks.zh_text: 这就回到了我的主要观点。

blocks.en_text: The growing concern about having kids in the climate crisis
blocks.zh_text: 人们对在气候危机中要孩子的日益担忧

blocks.en_text: is an urgent indicator of how hard-pressed people are feeling.
blocks.zh_text: 是一个紧迫的信号，说明人们感到多么压力山大。

blocks.en_text: Right now, students around the world are screaming for change
blocks.zh_text: 现在，世界各地的学生都在大声疾呼要求改变，

blocks.en_text: in the piercing voice of despair.
blocks.zh_text: 用绝望而刺耳的声音。

blocks.en_text: And the fact that we can see how we contribute to this problem
blocks.zh_text: 而我们能看清自己如何造成这个问题、

blocks.en_text: that makes us feel unsafe
blocks.zh_text: 如何让自己感到不安全，

blocks.en_text: is crazy-making in itself.
blocks.zh_text: 这本身就让人快疯了。

blocks.en_text: Climate change is all-encompassing
blocks.zh_text: 气候变化是无所不包的，

blocks.en_text: and so are the ways that it messes with our minds.
blocks.zh_text: 它扰乱我们心智的方式也是如此。

blocks.en_text: Many activists will tell you
blocks.zh_text: 很多活动人士会告诉你

blocks.en_text: that the best antidote to grief is activism.
blocks.zh_text: 化解悲伤最好的解药就是行动主义。

blocks.en_text: And some psychologists will tell you the answer can be found in therapy.
blocks.zh_text: 有些心理学家会告诉你，答案可以在心理治疗里找到。

blocks.en_text: Others believe the key is to imagine you're on your deathbed,
blocks.zh_text: 还有人相信，关键在于想象自己躺在临终的床上，

blocks.en_text: reflecting back on what's mattered the most in your life,
blocks.zh_text: 回想一生中什么最重要，

blocks.en_text: so you can identify what you should do more of now,
blocks.zh_text: 这样你就能看清现在应该多做什么，

blocks.en_text: with the time that you have left.
blocks.zh_text: 用你剩下的时间。

blocks.en_text: We need all these ideas, and more,
blocks.zh_text: 我们需要所有这些想法，还需要更多，

blocks.en_text: to take care of our innermost selves
blocks.zh_text: 来照顾我们内心最深处的自己，

blocks.en_text: as the environments we've known become more punishing towards us.
blocks.zh_text: 因为我们所熟悉的环境正变得越来越对我们不友好。

blocks.en_text: And whether you have children or not,
blocks.zh_text: 不管你有没有孩子，

blocks.en_text: we need to be honest about what is happening,
blocks.zh_text: 我们都得坦诚面对正在发生的事，

blocks.en_text: and what we owe one another.
blocks.zh_text: 以及我们彼此之间应尽的责任。

blocks.en_text: We cannot afford to treat
blocks.zh_text: 我们承担不起这样的代价：

blocks.en_text: the psychological impacts of climate change
blocks.zh_text: 把气候变化带来的心理影响

blocks.en_text: as some afterthought,
blocks.zh_text: 当成事后才想到的事，

blocks.en_text: because the other issues, of science, technology and the politics and economy,
blocks.zh_text: 因为科学、技术、政治和经济这些其他问题，

blocks.en_text: feel hard, while this somehow feels soft.
blocks.zh_text: 让人觉得很难，而这个问题却不知怎么让人觉得是软性的。

blocks.en_text: Mental health needs to be an integral part
blocks.zh_text: 心理健康必须成为

blocks.en_text: of any climate change survival strategy,
blocks.zh_text: 任何气候变化生存策略中不可或缺的一部分，

blocks.en_text: requiring funding, and ethics of equity and care,
blocks.zh_text: 需要资金投入，需要公平与关怀的伦理，

blocks.en_text: and widespread awareness.
blocks.zh_text: 还需要广泛的认知。

blocks.en_text: Because even if you're the most emotionally avoidant person on the planet,
blocks.zh_text: 因为就算你是这个星球上最会回避情绪的人，

blocks.en_text: there's no rug in the world that's big enough to sweep this up under.
blocks.zh_text: 世上也没有哪块地毯大到能把这件事扫到下面藏起来。

blocks.en_text: Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 谢谢。
